newsitem.title: THAILAND: Moslem "bandits" suspected of killing four workers.
newsitem.headline: Moslem "bandits" suspected of killing four workers.

text.p: Armed Moslem bandits are suspected of shooting and killing four rubber plantation workers in a southern town on the Thai-Malaysian border, Thai police said on Thursday.

Police said a group of about 15 armed men stormed a workers' hut late on Wednesday in Tharn Namthip village in Yala province about 1,400 km (840 miles) south of Bangkok, opening fire with M-16 rifles and killing four men."
The village is just a few metres from the border with Malaysia.
"We believe that Moslem bandits were responsible for the massacre but we do not have many details," one police official said.

A handful of Moslems bandits remain from the now-defunct Pattani United Liberation Organisation (PULO) which was formed in the 1960s to fight for the separation of the Moslem-dominated provinces in southern Thailand.

The PULO was disbanded after the government declared a general amnesty in 1984 but some former members have become bandits and earn their living through extortion and by blackmailing local businessmen, police sources said.
Police said Wednesday's attack could be in retaliation for an incident last month when four Moslem bandits were killed by Thai soldiers in a neighbouring province.
